subject: science
title: Dig Into Soil
about: Comparing soils: sand, clay and humus, which holds water, which drains, and what good soil gives a plant (ESS.1.2.2). NC wants children to test local soil samples; these cards hold the ideas behind the test.
tip: Fill two cups, one with sand and one with garden soil, pour in water and watch which one holds it longer.

cards.q: Soil from a beach and soil from a garden are...
cards.note: Soil is different in different places.
Nutrients are things in soil that help plants grow.
Plants grow best in soil that holds water and has nutrients.

cards.q: Which three things can be in soil?
cards.note: Soil can have sand, clay and humus in it.

cards.q: Which has bigger grains, sand or clay?
cards.note: Clay grains are too tiny to see one by one.

cards.q: Which one does water run through fastest, sand or clay?
cards.note: Big sand grains leave big gaps for water to run through.

cards.q: Which holds water longer, sand or clay?
cards.note: Clay retains water. Sand lets it drain away.

cards.q: What is the dark, crumbly part of soil made from rotted leaves?
cards.note: Rotted leaves and plants turn into humus.

cards.q: Which one feels gritty, like tiny rocks?
cards.note: Sand grains are tiny bits of rock.

cards.q: Which one feels sticky and smooth when it is wet?
cards.note: People shape wet clay into pots and bricks.

cards.q: How do you find out which soil holds the most water?
cards.note: Scientists test things to find out. They do not just guess.

cards.q: Same seeds, same water, same light, but not the same soil. One plant grew taller. What made the difference?
cards.note: A fair test changes only one thing.
Soil is tiny bits of broken rock mixed with rotted plants.
